speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of the right flank pain and when the hematuria first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any nausea, vomiting, or fever, and does the pain radiate toward your groin? Also, have you noticed any difficulty urinating or a change in urine flow?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a personal or family history of kidney stones, and have you experienced any fever or chills recently? I would also like to check for costovertebral angle tenderness during a physical exam.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan rules out stones, but the positive leukocyte esterase and WBCs suggest an infection. Do you have any burning sensation during urination, increased urgency, or lower abdominal pain? I will also request a urine culture to identify the specific bacteria.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the hematuria and pyuria with a negative CT scan, I need to rule out malignancy or interstitial cystitis. Do you experience urinary frequency or nocturia, and have you noticed any weight loss or fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine_Culture: NORMAL READINGS. IMAGES: Intravenous_Pyelogram: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms medullary cysts, which is diagnostic for Medullary Sponge Kidney. This condition often presents with hematuria and recurrent urinary tract infections due to urine stasis in the cysts. DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney
